title: Dataset grants + cache layer for analytics endpoints and usage views
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add dataset-level grants and an authorization-aware caching layer to analytics HTTP endpoints and downstream usage views. Current behavior allows project-scoped queries to return rows the caller shouldn’t see when queries are served from the analytics cache or from pre-aggregated tables. This ticket implements enforcement on three levels: (1) compile-time query tagging and plan validation, (2) query-time row-level filter application for both live and cached responses, and (3) a cache key strategy that includes effective grants so we never serve cached results to principals without access.
acceptance_criteria: All analytics endpoints must attach a dataset_grants token to every query plan before execution
Caching layer includes a serialized granularity of grants in cache keys and refuses to serve cached payloads when the request principal lacks grants
Unit and integration tests covering horizontal and vertical sharding cases with at least 95% branch coverage for grant enforcement paths
No performance regression >10% p95 latency for common 'usage by model' queries in staging compared with baseline (allowable with caching disabled for initial rollout)
Audit logs emitted for any denied cached fetch attempts and stored for 90 days
Console admin page shows a readout of active grant-cache mismatches and provides a one-click invalidate for affected cache keys
tasks: Design cache key schema that immutably encodes: principal id, dataset grants hash, time-window, and query fingerprint
Add grant-resolution module that resolves dataset grants from RBAC store (with TTL) and returns canonical grant set
Instrument query planner to tag plans with dataset_grants and inject safe WHERE clauses for row-level filtering
Modify cache read path to verify grants hash against request resolve and fallthrough to live execution on mismatch
Write integration tests using synthetic multi-tenant dataset with cross-project access patterns
Add observability metrics: cache_hit_by_grant, cache_miss_grant_mismatch, grant_resolution_latency
Create console-frontend ticket to surface grant mismatch alerts and an invalidate action (PM follow-up)
Submit PR and coordinate security review and performance sign-off
technical_notes: Trade-offs: including grants in cache keys increases cache cardinality. To mitigate, we will use a grant-hash computed from normalized grant tuples (resource, role) and support wildcard consolidation for identical grant sets.

We considered enforcing grants only at read-time via an API gateway layer but rejected it because pre-aggregations (materialized tables) would still risk leaking rows; planner-level predicates are required for safety.
Grant TTL: choose conservative default of 5m to balance cache reuse and permission change propagation. Add explicit cache invalidation hook when RBAC changes are committed.
Row filtering: use index-friendly predicate patterns where possible (e.g., project_id IN (...)) to avoid full scans on large tables.

Fail-open vs fail-closed: system will fail-closed for cached grant mismatches (i.e., re-run query without cache) but fail-open for grant-resolution service timeout only after circuit-breaker threshold — security team requested conservative behavior for outages.
